Project Summary:
Rocker Launch is an interactive, multi-stage space mission simulation game designed to make aerospace engineering concepts accessible and engaging.

What did you develop?
We developed a web-based simulation platform where users design spacecraft, manage critical resources (such as fuel, mass, and components), and make high-stakes tactical decisions across distinct mission levels, including a Mars sample-return scenario.

How it addresses the challenge?
The project addresses the complexity of space mission planning by translating abstract engineering trade-offs and orbital mechanics into interactive, decision-driven gameplay, allowing players to balance constraints against mission success in real time.

Why it is important?
It fosters critical thinking, strategic resource management, and STEM engagement, serving as an intuitive educational tool that inspires a deeper interest in space exploration and mission architecture.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Rocker Launch is an interactive, web-based space mission simulation game that guides players through the complexities of aerospace engineering and mission planning.

  • How it works: Players step into the role of a mission controller. They start by choosing a mission objective (such as the Mars Sample Mission), designing and configuring their spacecraft's modular components and resource loads (like fuel and payload mass), and managing critical trade-offs. Once the design is locked, they launch the mission, where their decisions directly dictate whether the spacecraft succeeds or fails based on real-world simulated constraints.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Educational Value: Translates complex orbital mechanics, physics, and aerospace trade-offs into an intuitive, gamified experience.
  • Skill Enhancement: Fosters critical thinking, strategic problem-solving, and efficient resource allocation under pressure.
  • Accessibility: Built entirely for the web, allowing users to access, test, and engage with space science concepts instantly without heavy software installations.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The primary goal is to ignite curiosity and engagement in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) fields—particularly space systems engineering—among students and tech enthusiasts. By bridging the gap between abstract academic physics and engaging interactive gameplay, the project aims to inspire the next generation of space innovators, researchers, and developers to explore aerospace mission architecture.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Languages & Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for structuring the interactive interface, managing game logic, and handling dynamic user inputs.
  • Hosting & Deployment: GitHub Pages for seamless, reliable web deployment and version control.
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code and a modern web browser environment for rapid prototyping, debugging, and UI styling.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Gamified Engineering: Instead of static tutorials or complex enterprise software, Rocker Launch turns critical engineering decisions into an engaging narrative and interactive challenge.
  • Immersive Design: Features a clean, modern, space-themed aesthetic with intuitive navigation that mimics real mission control dashboards, delivering a polished user experience from the moment the browser opens.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • User Experience (UX) vs. Realism: Balancing scientific accuracy (such as mass and fuel constraints) with simple, accessible gameplay mechanics so players are challenged without feeling overwhelmed.
  • Modularity & Scalability: Designing the game architecture with a multi-level structure (the_levels.html, level modules) to allow easy expansion with new mission types, challenges, and planets in the future.
  • Performance: Ensuring lightweight, fast-loading frontend execution so the simulation runs smoothly across different devices and screen sizes.
